pages.text: <!DOCTYPE html> The Apa Experience - Apa Aesthetic What We Do The Apa Experience Cosmetic Dentistry Porcelain Veneers Smile Makeover ProcessWho We Are About Us Dr. Apa Our Team Our Locations Brand PartnersOur Work Before/After Photos Patient Testimonials Buzz BlogSchedule a Consultation The Apa Experience REDEFINING EXCELLENCE Apa Aesthetic is the unrivaled dental destination for want-based treatment and life-changing results. About the Apa Experience It only takes a moment to realize Apa Aesthetic is no ordinary dentist’s office. Apa Aesthetic is an unparalleled disrupter in an industry that has for far too long relied on one-size-fits-all solutions. Led by Dr. Michael Apa, we have set a new standard for veneers—one that customizes every step to produce the most natural, one-of-a-kind results for every client. Apa Aesthetic smile makeover patients are assessed holistically and enjoy access to treatments outside of the cosmetic umbrella. From cleanings to fillings, we do it all under one roof. What to Expect At Apa Aesthetic, we continually challenge the status quo, finding new ways to improve our treatment plans, promote oral health and elevate the world of dentistry. STEP INTO COMFORT. Our offices reflect our standard of care. Museum-worthy art adorns the walls, while a client comfort list offers access to a cashmere blanket, noise-canceling headphones, a ceiling-mounted TV and an array of CBD confections. CONNECT AND COMMUNICATE. From your smile makeover to aftercare, we prioritize open communication. At each step, we discuss your goals, present treatment options and welcome your feedback. This collaborative approach promises final results that align with your expectations, for a smile you’ll love. EXPERIENCE CUSTOMIZATION. Dr. Apa has assembled the world's most accomplished ceramists, in technical expertise and artistic talent, to deliver one-of-a-kind smiles. Watch as our ceramists hand-craft porcelain veneers in our glass-enclosed state-of-the-art lab. ENJOY LIFELONG CARE. The end of your smile makeover marks the beginning of your new journey with us, aftercare. We have the training and tools to ensure the health and longevity of your treatment. Plan to see us quarterly or, at a minimum, annually for a seamless aftercare experience. headings: Experience a Smile Makeover For Yourself
pages.text: <!DOCTYPE html> Smile Makeover Process - Apa Aesthetic What We Do The Apa Experience Cosmetic Dentistry Porcelain Veneers Smile Makeover ProcessWho We Are About Us Dr. Apa Our Team Our Locations Brand PartnersOur Work Before/After Photos Patient Testimonials Buzz BlogSchedule a Consultation Smile Makeover Process Designing the Smile for You Together, we are creating something emotional, something that lights up our patients' faces — and their lives. APA AESTHETIC'S UNIQUE APPROACH We deliver highly-customized results that follow the same proven process. Our workflow has been fine-tuned over our 25-year history. The journey begins with a consultation. THE SMILE MAKEOVER PROCESS CollapseThe ConsultationDuring this 90-minute appointment, we will review your dental and medical history, conduct a thorough examination of your teeth, gums and mouth, and take x-rays, scans and photos. You will have the opportunity to detail your goals and ask questions before your dentist determines the best treatment plan to achieve your ideal smile. ExpandThe Prep Appointment - 4 HrsEnjoy a Smart TV, noise-cancelling headphones, cozy blanket and CBD confections. During this working appointment, your teeth are shaped in preparation for veneers. The process involves dental anesthetics, custom molds of the teeth, and the hand-design and placement of your temporary smile. ExpandThe Initial Post-Op Appointment - 1.5 HrsIt’s time to talk about the color, size and fit of your temporary smile. We will make on-the-spot adjustments to refine the design before collecting your signature of approval and taking records for our in-house lab. ExpandThe Insert Appointment - 4 HrsEnjoy a Smart TV, noise-cancelling headphones, cozy blanket and CBD confections. Your custom, hand-layered porcelain restorations took two weeks to complete. Now it’s time to remove your temporary smile and insert your new, permanent smile. You will be numb for your comfort. ExpandThe Final Post-Op Appointment - 1.5 HrsWhile we check your bite during the insert, we have you return for precision. We take final records, photograph your new smile and scan for a nightguard. headings: A SMILE MAKEOVER AT APA AESTHETIC
pages.text: <!DOCTYPE html> Dr. Michael Apa - Apa Aesthetic What We Do The Apa Experience Cosmetic Dentistry Porcelain Veneers Smile Makeover ProcessWho We Are About Us Dr. Apa Our Team Our Locations Brand PartnersOur Work Before/After Photos Patient Testimonials Buzz BlogSchedule a Consultation Dr. Apa Dr. Michael Apa, DDS Founder, Apa Aesthetic Michael Apa is an internationally-renowned dentist, specializing in minimally invasive cosmetic dentistry and smile makeovers. He earned recognition as the dentist to the stars, having treated Jennifer Lopez, Kendall and Kylie Jenner, Uma Thurman, Kyle Richards, the Olsen Twins, and more. Early Life and Education Apa was born and raised in upstate New York and, from the age of five, aspired to be a dentist. He earned his Bachelor of Science degree (B.S.) in Biology from LeMoyne College and his Doctor of Dental Surgery (DDS) from New York University College of Dentistry, where he established the first undergraduate aesthetics program and opened a dedicated clinical education space bearing his name. Career After graduation, Apa fulfilled his dream of working alongside Dr. Larry Rosenthal as an associate in his New York City office. In 2004, Apa became a partner at the practice and, in 2014, its sole proprietor. Apa is the pioneer of Facial Aesthetic Design (FAD), a new approach to crafting and fitting porcelain veneers that considers a patient’s facial framework when developing a smile treatment plan. In 2015, Apa opened an office in Dubai, under the name Apa Aesthetic. Los Angeles and Miami followed, in 2019 and 2024, respectively. Apa is the founder of Apa Beauty, a line of oral care cosmetics, introduced in 2014. Apa is a member of the American Academy of Cosmetic Dentistry (AACD), American Dental Association (ADA), and Academy of General Dentistry (AGD). He is also on the Editorial Advisory Board for the Journal of Implant and Advanced Clinical Dentistry and on the Leaders Board for Dentistry Today. Apa is an assistant Clinical Professor at the New York University College of Dentistry in the Aesthetics Department. He is also a senior clinical instructor for Aesthetic Advantage hands on Continuum at The Rosenthal Institute at New York University College of Dentistry Awards Apa was the recipient of the 2007 AACD Cosmetic Dentistry Award for outstanding performance in the first five years of practice. Media In 2015, Apa launched his YouTube series “Dr. Apa,” which followed him as he built his Dubai practice. Apa has appeared on numerous television programs and amassed an Instagram following of over 600k people, with whom he shares his rigorous morning workouts, handsome wardrobe and, of course, remarkable before and after patient photos. About Our Brand Partnerships NYU College of Dentistry In Fall 2023, Dr. Apa announced a historic partnership with his alma mater, New York University College of Dentistry, to refine and elevate its programs in aesthetic dentistry and enhance the student experience. Dr. Apa proudly established the "Apa Suite," a state-of-the-art clinical education space and the first permanent home for the Apa Advanced Clinical Fellowship in Aesthetics and the Apa Honors Program in Aesthetics. Phone 212-998-8700 Website: https://dental.nyu.edu/patientcare/aesthetic-dentistry.html View this post on Instagram A post shared by Michael Apa (@doctorapa) View this post on Instagram A post shared by Michael Apa (@doctorapa) View this post on Instagram A post shared by Michael Apa (@doctorapa) View this post on Instagram A post shared by Michael Apa (@doctorapa) CUNY School of Public Health In 2021, Apa Aesthetic pledged a groundbreaking investment in CUNY SPH to establish a new academic focus on the intersection of oral and population health. The partnership includes a scholarship fund for 10 students each year. pages.description: When do you fix a gummy smile? The phrase “long in the tooth” originates from the idea that receding gums make teeth appear longer and faces look older. A slight gummy smile – up to 3 millimeters – can be seen as a hallmark of youth. This patient’s primary concern…
pages.text: <!DOCTYPE html> Fixing a Gummy Smile - Before & After - Apa Aesthetic What We Do The Apa Experience Cosmetic Dentistry Porcelain Veneers Smile Makeover ProcessWho We Are About Us Dr. Apa Our Team Our Locations Brand PartnersOur Work Before/After Photos Patient Testimonials Buzz BlogSchedule a Consultation Patient Female When do you fix a gummy smile? The phrase “long in the tooth” originates from the idea that receding gums make teeth appear longer and faces look older. A slight gummy smile – up to 3 millimeters – can be seen as a hallmark of youth. This patient’s primary concern was not gum visibility, but rather gum asymmetry. She also wanted to address the narrowness of her smile and old fillings in her front teeth. Our approach focused on creating harmony in her gum line while slightly reducing the gumminess. We had the opportunity to reduce a lot, but favored a more conservative approach to preserve the spirit of her natural smile. By refining her teeth and gums, we crafted a smile that feels authentic – like it was hers all along. pages.text: <!DOCTYPE html> Adult Orthodontic Issues to a Revitalized Smile - Apa Aesthetic What We Do The Apa Experience Cosmetic Dentistry Porcelain Veneers Smile Makeover ProcessWho We Are About Us Dr. Apa Our Team Our Locations Brand PartnersOur Work Before/After Photos Patient Testimonials Buzz BlogSchedule a Consultation Patient Female Following orthodontic treatment, this patient was left with bite contact only on her front teeth, which causes gradual damage over time. Adults considering Invisalign should seek treatment from a highly qualified orthodontist with extensive experience in adult orthodontics and commit to completing the process fully to avoid further complications. This patient completed her orthodontic treatment but developed a bite that only engaged her front teeth, leaving her unable to properly use her back teeth for chewing. The excessive pressure on her front teeth caused gum and bone deterioration, leading to recession and the appearance of black triangles. The focus of this case was less on aesthetics and more on re-establishing a stable and functional occlusion. We placed minimally prepped veneers on the lower teeth and overlaid the back teeth to increase their height, providing a strong foundational bite. To address her reverse smile and enhance her appearance, we slightly lengthened her front teeth and selected a fresher, more vibrant color, resulting in both improved function and a revitalized smile. When implants are positioned improperly, it can lead to the loss of the gum triangle between the teeth, making the implants appear thick and bulky, regardless of…
pages.text: <!DOCTYPE html> Correcting Improper Implants after Fall - Apa Aesthetic What We Do The Apa Experience Cosmetic Dentistry Porcelain Veneers Smile Makeover ProcessWho We Are About Us Dr. Apa Our Team Our Locations Brand PartnersOur Work Before/After Photos Patient Testimonials Buzz BlogSchedule a Consultation Patient Male This case presented significant challenges. Several years ago, the patient fainted and fell, resulting in broken front teeth that were replaced with implants. When implants are positioned improperly, it can lead to the loss of the gum triangle between the teeth, making the implants appear thick and bulky, regardless of the quality of the ceramic. We redesigned his smile with a new bridge on the existing implants, incorporating pink ceramic to simulate the lost gum tissue. This approach was a pivotal improvement, as it created the illusion of thinner, more natural-looking teeth. The result was a more individualized smile, with less focus on the front of the mouth, for a harmonious and aesthetic outcome. pages.description: This patient had naturally good teeth throughout her life and reached her early 70s before seeking cosmetic dentistry. After thoroughly researching her options, she chose us with one clear goal: results that looked completely natural. pages.text: <!DOCTYPE html> Aging Patient's Smile Adjusted to be Youthful and Vibrant - Apa Aesthetic What We Do The Apa Experience Cosmetic Dentistry Porcelain Veneers Smile Makeover ProcessWho We Are About Us Dr. Apa Our Team Our Locations Brand PartnersOur Work Before/After Photos Patient Testimonials Buzz BlogSchedule a Consultation Patient Female This patient had naturally good teeth throughout her life and reached her early 70s before seeking cosmetic dentistry. After thoroughly researching her options, she chose us with one clear goal: results that looked completely natural. Our treatment plan included subtle rotations in the ceramic on her lower teeth to preserve authenticity, as well as addressing her crossbite by properly aligning the upper and lower teeth. She wanted to enhance her smile to look and feel her best – a transformation we were thrilled to provide. A closer look reveals a classic example of being “long in the tooth.” While upper teeth are typically about one-third larger than lower teeth, recession on her bottom teeth made them appear disproportionately large. To restore balance, we carefully adjusted her bite by shortening the lower teeth and lengthening the upper teeth while preserving as much natural tooth structure as possible. By showing more of her upper teeth, her smile now appears youthful and vibrant, reflecting the best version of herself. pages.title: New York City Cosmetic Dentist - Apa Aesthetic
pages.description: Apa Aesthetic New York combines artistry and precision to deliver exceptional dental transformations. Redefine your smile with personalized, elite care in NYC.
pages.text: <!DOCTYPE html> New York City Cosmetic Dentist - Apa Aesthetic What We Do The Apa Experience Cosmetic Dentistry Porcelain Veneers Smile Makeover ProcessWho We Are About Us Dr. Apa Our Team Our Locations Brand PartnersOur Work Before/After Photos Patient Testimonials Buzz BlogSchedule a Consultation New York 30 E 76TH ST. Floor 5 NEW YORK, NY 10021 212.794.9600 DOCTORS AT PRACTICE: Dr. Michael ApaDr. Clement KairouzDr. Nick MavrostomosDr. Nicolas AguileraDr. Larry RosenthalDr. Andi-Jean MiroDr. Vince AvalloneDr. Graig Fischgrund New York Cosmetic Dentist Please complete the short form below to schedule a call with an Apa Aesthetic patient coordinator. Our coordinators are trained to answer your questions, understand your treatment goals and explain our signature Facial Aesthetic Design and Smile Makeover services. After this preliminary call, we can arrange a virtual or in-person consultation with one of our doctors. Locations Form - PipeDrive Test "*" indicates required fields FAQs ExpandWhere is Apa Aesthetic’s New York office located?Apa Aesthetic New York is located at 30 East 76th Street, Floor 5, New York, NY 10021, on Manhattan’s Upper East Side. The office can be reached at 212-794-9600. ExpandWhat are the hours for the New York office?Apa Aesthetic New York is open Monday through Thursday from 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. and Friday from 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. The office is closed on Saturday and Sunday. Holiday and summer hours may vary, so patients should contact the office before visiting. ExpandIs Apa Aesthetic New York accepting new patients?Yes. Apa Aesthetic New York welcomes new patients seeking cosmetic treatment, including personalized smile makeovers, porcelain veneers, and the replacement or revision of cosmetic dental work completed elsewhere. Apa Aesthetic does not accept new patients seeking standalone routine general dentistry. Once a patient commits to cosmetic treatment, they have access to the general, preventive, and restorative care needed to support their treatment and maintain their smile over time. New patients may request either an in-person or virtual consultation. ExpandWhich dentists practice at Apa Aesthetic New York?The New York cosmetic dentistry team includes Dr. Michael Apa, Dr. Clement Kairouz, Dr. Nick Mavrostomos, Dr. Nicolas Aguilera, Dr. Larry Rosenthal, Dr. Andi-Jean Miro, and Dr. Vince Avallone. Periodontist Dr. Graig Fischgrund is also part of the New York team. Patients may request a particular provider when contacting the practice. Treatment needs, provider specialization, appointment availability, and scheduling will help determine the provider best suited to each case. ExpandDoes Dr. Michael Apa see patients in New York City?Yes. Dr. Michael Apa sees patients at Apa Aesthetic New York, and patients may request him when contacting the practice. Appointment availability may vary. Dr. Apa is the founder of Apa Aesthetic and is known for his highly individualized approach to porcelain veneers, smile makeovers, and Facial Aesthetic Design. His approach considers the entire face—not only the teeth—to create a smile that feels balanced, functional, and authentic to the individual. ExpandWhat services does Apa Aesthetic New York offer?Apa Aesthetic New York specializes in cosmetic and restorative dentistry. Services include complete smile makeovers, porcelain veneers, veneer replacement and revision, dental crowns, dental bridges, dental implants, gum contouring, crown lengthening, restorative treatment, bite and functional rehabilitation, and teeth whitening. For patients undergoing cosmetic treatment, the team also addresses the oral health needed to support that work, including examinations, X-rays, professional cleanings, fillings, preventive care, and necessary restorative treatment. ExpandIs Apa Aesthetic New York a general dentistry practice?Apa Aesthetic New York is first and foremost a cosmetic dental practice and does not accept new patients seeking standalone routine general dentistry. Once a patient commits to cosmetic treatment, they have access to the general, restorative, and preventive care needed before, during, and after their smile makeover. This allows the team to create cosmetic work on a healthy foundation and continue caring for it over the long term. ExpandDoes Apa Aesthetic New York offer porcelain veneers and veneer replacement?Yes. Apa Aesthetic New York provides individually designed porcelain veneers as part of personalized smile makeovers. The team also treats patients who want to replace or revise aging, damaged, bulky, opaque, or unnatural-looking veneers and other cosmetic dental work completed elsewhere. Revision cases require careful evaluation of the underlying teeth, previous tooth preparation, existing restorations, materials, and bite before treatment is recommended. ExpandWhat makes Apa Aesthetic New York different from other cosmetic dentistry practices in NYC?Every Apa Aesthetic smile is designed for the individual—not around a standardized idea of perfection. The team considers the teeth in relation to the lips, facial structure, bite, expression, and movement. Treatment combines facially driven smile design, conservative clinical techniques, handcrafted porcelain restorations, an in-house dental laboratory, and comprehensive long-term care. ExpandWhat happens during a cosmetic dentistry consultation at Apa Aesthetic New York?The process begins with a patient coordinator learning more about your concerns, goals, and preferred provider. The team can then arrange either a virtual or in-person consultation with one of the New York dentists. During the clinical consultation, your provider will review your dental and medical history, examine your teeth, gums, bite, and existing dental work, and discuss what you would like to change. Clinical records may include photographs, digital scans, X-rays, and other diagnostic information. Your provider will then explain the recommended treatment options, timeline, and cost. ExpandDoes Apa Aesthetic New York have an in-house dental laboratory?Yes. Apa Aesthetic New York has an in-house laboratory where dentists and master ceramists collaborate throughout the smile makeover process. More complex cases may require preliminary treatment, additional visits, or a longer timeline. headings: SEE THE LATEST FROM DR. ANDI
Follow Dr. Andi-Jean Miro on Instagram
pages.text: <!DOCTYPE html> Dr. Andi-Jean Miro - Apa Aesthetic What We Do The Apa Experience Cosmetic Dentistry Porcelain Veneers Smile Makeover ProcessWho We Are About Us Dr. Apa Our Team Our Locations Brand PartnersOur Work Before/After Photos Patient Testimonials Buzz BlogSchedule a Consultation Dr. Andi-Jean Miro Location Los Angeles, New York Position Dentist Dr. Andi-Jean Miro is a cosmetic dentist, educator, and entrepreneur based between Los Angeles and New York City. Since 2015, she has been a key part of Apa Aesthetic, where she is the practice’s only female cosmetic dentist. Specializing in high-end cosmetic dentistry, porcelain veneers, smile makeovers, and facially driven smile aesthetics, Dr. Andi is known for creating refined, natural-looking transformations that enhance the entire face — not just the teeth. A graduate of New York University College of Dentistry, Dr. Andi completed an advanced clinical concentration in Aesthetic Dentistry before completing her general residency at NYU Lutheran in Brooklyn. Her foundation in both clinical dentistry and aesthetic design shaped the way she approaches every case: with precision, restraint, and an understanding that a smile should never be designed in isolation. Dr. Andi’s philosophy is rooted in one belief: great cosmetic dentistry should not look generic. Every smile is designed around the patient’s face, lips, bite, skin tone, personality, and long-term aesthetic goals. Her goal is never to create a “veneer smile,” but to create a smile that looks elevated, natural, and completely specific to the person wearing it. Today, Dr. Andi treats patients between Apa Aesthetic Beverly Hills and Apa Aesthetic New York, creating custom porcelain veneer transformations and smile makeovers for patients seeking results that feel personal, balanced, and refined. With access to Apa Aesthetic’s onsite ceramics laboratory and master ceramists, each case is customized with an exceptional level of detail — from shape and proportion to texture, translucency, color, and facial harmony. In addition to her clinical work, Dr. Andi is the founder of Stribe, a dental education company created to teach elite-level cosmetic dentistry to dentists around the world. Through Stribe and its signature hands-on course, Art of Ceramic, she educates doctors on porcelain veneer techniques, case planning, preparation design, lab communication, temporaries, cementation, and the details that separate average dentistry from exceptional dentistry. Her work lives at the intersection of beauty, science, artistry, and education — creating dentistry that does not announce itself, but makes the patient look like the best, most refined version of themselves. pages.text: <!DOCTYPE html> Fixing Failing Veneers with New Treatment - Apa Aesthetic What We Do The Apa Experience Cosmetic Dentistry Porcelain Veneers Smile Makeover ProcessWho We Are About Us Dr. Apa Our Team Our Locations Brand PartnersOur Work Before/After Photos Patient Testimonials Buzz BlogSchedule a Consultation Patient Female This patient presented with eight veneers previously placed without addressing her gummy smile. The previous treatment attempted to achieve “golden proportions,” which we regard as a guideline rather than a standard. In this case, prioritizing those proportions resulted in teeth that were disproportionately long. By the time the patient came to us, her veneers were 10 years old and exhibited signs of failure. The black discoloration at the margins indicated microleakage. Additionally, there was noticeable gum swelling, evidenced by a red ring around the tissue, caused by biologic width impingement from excessively thick margins. We removed the old veneers and redesigned her smile. The incisal edge position was shortened to prevent elongation of her face, and we broadened the arch for a more balanced appearance. We placed 12 new veneers on the upper arch and 10 on the lower, ensuring precise margins. In the after photo, the transformation is clear—the gums have transitioned from an unhealthy purple-red to a healthy light pink, signifying restored oral health. The patient had upper veneers done elsewhere. Due to her flared lower teeth, the upper veneers were positioned too far forward, resulting in the appearance of protrusion or “buck teeth.” Additionally, the previous treatment failed to address the narrowness of her upper arch. We approached this case with a comprehensive treatment plan, which is essential for achieving optimal results. By veneering the lower teeth, we corrected their flare and brought them into proper alignment. We widened the upper arch and replaced the existing veneers with new ones that were thinner and designed to put her teeth in a more natural position. The new veneers were crafted with greater gradation and translucency, creating a natural aesthetic. This meticulous attention to detail eliminated the appearance of protrusion and resulted in a beautifully balanced smile. pages.text: <!DOCTYPE html> Comprehensive Veneer Replacement and Gum Treatment - Apa Aesthetic What We Do The Apa Experience Cosmetic Dentistry Porcelain Veneers Smile Makeover ProcessWho We Are About Us Dr. Apa Our Team Our Locations Brand PartnersOur Work Before/After Photos Patient Testimonials Buzz BlogSchedule a Consultation Patient Female This patient presented with old veneers, a challenging bite, and significant gum recession. When her veneers were initially placed, the gums were intact, but over time, they receded. The pronounced recession was due to a heavy bite on the front teeth, leading to traumatic occlusion. The excessive pressure pushed the teeth forward, ultimately causing the bone and gum to recede. In restoring this case, we took a comprehensive approach to address her lower teeth, bite alignment, and gum recession. We closed the black triangles caused by the recession and enhanced the ceramic to achieve a more natural and lifelike appearance. By balancing her bite, we significantly reduced the risk of further recession, ensuring a healthier and more stable long-term outcome. pages.description: This patient’s original smile reflected the natural effects of aging. She was frequently complimented on her teeth and many wondered why she would seek treatment. She had minimal wear and was generally happy with her appearance. However, she wanted to address the grayish tone of her teeth. Over time, natural…
pages.text: <!DOCTYPE html> Adjusting Aging Teeth Color - Apa Aesthetic What We Do The Apa Experience Cosmetic Dentistry Porcelain Veneers Smile Makeover ProcessWho We Are About Us Dr. Apa Our Team Our Locations Brand PartnersOur Work Before/After Photos Patient Testimonials Buzz BlogSchedule a Consultation Patient Female This patient’s original smile reflected the natural effects of aging. She was frequently complimented on her teeth and many wondered why she would seek treatment. She had minimal wear and was generally happy with her appearance. However, she wanted to address the grayish tone of her teeth. Over time, natural wear, grinding, and the shrinking of dental nerves reduce blood supply to the teeth, resulting in a gradual gray discoloration. Our objective was not to dramatically alter her smile but to subtly enhance it while preserving its character. Using her natural tooth shapes as a blueprint, we corrected minor shifting and revitalized the color, transitioning from a gray-white tone to a vibrant yellow-white, creating a more youthful and refreshed appearance. pages.title: The Measure of Excellence - Apa Aesthetic
pages.description: Excellence is never a final destination; it’s a culture defined by an unwavering commitment to continuous refinement, reflected in every person behind the work. As he pushes his aesthetic vision forward, Dr. Apa has assembled a world-class team of ceramists from around the world, each with unique talents and unrivaled…
pages.text: <!DOCTYPE html> The Measure of Excellence - Apa Aesthetic What We Do The Apa Experience Cosmetic Dentistry Porcelain Veneers Smile Makeover ProcessWho We Are About Us Dr. Apa Our Team Our Locations Brand PartnersOur Work Before/After Photos Patient Testimonials Buzz BlogSchedule a Consultation The Measure of Excellence Aug 19, 2026 Excellence is never a final destination; it’s a culture defined by an unwavering commitment to continuous refinement, reflected in every person behind the work. As he pushes his aesthetic vision forward, Dr. Apa has assembled a world-class team of ceramists from around the world, each with unique talents and unrivaled technical precision. Technique alone is merely the point of entry, while artistry demands a profound sensitivity to our aesthetic language. Mastery in ceramic design relies on subtle dimensions of form, color, texture, proportion, and light. Within our team, individual instincts manifest in different ways. Every Apa Aesthetic ceramist brings a distinct, indefinable “it” factor to the bench – a singular vision of character, depth, or anatomical harmony. Their individuality becomes a source of learning. Our ceramists continually turn to one another, studying how another artist sees, interprets, and solves a case. They also learn deeply from the clinician they work with most. Over time, that close working relationship creates a shared language: the ceramist gains a more nuanced understanding of the doctor’s biological and spatial perspective, expanding what they thought possible through design. Exchange extends across the broader team. Rather than isolating expertise within individual specialties, we allow knowledge to move between our team members, using each perspective to sharpen the others. When people operating at an elite level remain open to one another’s thinking, constructive feedback inspires rather than threatens. Individual mastery compounds, and excellence evolves into collective intelligence. A Global Infrastructure Apa Aesthetic operates as a global practice. Not a collection of individual offices across continents, but a seamlessly integrated technical ecosystem operating as one. Fully dedicated in-house labs operate within all four of our locations, New York, Los Angeles, Miami, and Dubai, guided by a centralized lab management team based out of our New York flagship. Our infrastructure delivers a level of consistency and personalized continuity rarely found in modern dentistry: Bespoke Ceramist Pairing: Cases are intentionally paired with the in-house ceramist whose artistic strengths and “it” factor best align with your functional and aesthetic goals. While we prioritize working with a ceramist in your local clinic, but our global network allows us to look beyond geography when another ceramist is uniquely suited to your case. Direct Chairside Alignment: Having master ceramists just steps away from the operatories allows for real-time shade mapping, subtle light-reflection analysis, and precise micro-adjustments directly alongside your doctor. Unified Quality Standards: Centralized oversight from our New York management team guarantees that every restoration adheres to the exact same uncompromising benchmark, regardless of which location or ceramist crafts it. By eliminating third-party commercial labs, we remove the divide between clinical vision and technical execution, ensuring the final result is as seamless as it is bespoke. Where Technology Meets the Hand We often say that having an in-house lab is not enough. The value of the lab depends on the people within it, the systems that connect them, and the leadership that ensures each part works together. The most advanced tools only become meaningful in the hands of people who know how—and when—to use them. That philosophy comes to life at the bench. Dr. Apa and the Apa Aesthetic lab pioneered the hybrid model; the strategic combination of the accuracy and control of digital technology with the sensitivity and judgment of the human hand. We don’t consider digital and analog processes opposing philosophies. Each offers something the other cannot. Digital technology gives our team extraordinary control over information, allowing our clinicians and ceramists to capture, study, communicate, and reproduce dimensions with remarkable accuracy. Across a global practice, information can travel between locations without losing the detail necessary to make highly nuanced decisions. But precision is not the same as perception. There is a point in every case where measurement gives way to the eye and the hand. The subtle transition of translucency through an incisal edge, the irregularity of surface texture, the way light moves through ceramic, or the almost imperceptible adjustment that makes a restoration belong to a face—these decisions resist standardization. Our process moves deliberately between both worlds. Technology establishes control; the hand introduces character. Digital tools allow us to see and execute with greater accuracy, while analog artistry allows us to interpret what we see. Neither replaces the other. Together, they give our providers and ceramists greater freedom to craft a smile that is uniquely yours. Apa Aesthetic Consultations Experience the Apa Aesthetic standard for yourself. Schedule a consultation at Apa Aesthetic in New York, Los Angeles, Miami or Dubai and discover asn approach to aesthetic dentistry shaped by the same pursuit of excellence, artistry and continuous refinement. headings: How Long Do Porcelain Veneers Last?
The Lifespan of Porcelain Veneers Isn’t Defined by a Calendar
A Smile Makeover Is an Investment in Yourself
Porcelain Veneers Offer More Than Cosmetic Improvement
How to Make Porcelain Veneers Last
Why Long-Term Relationships Matter in Cosmetic Dentistry
pages.text: <!DOCTYPE html> How Long Do Porcelain Veneers Last? - Apa Aesthetic What We Do The Apa Experience Cosmetic Dentistry Porcelain Veneers Smile Makeover ProcessWho We Are About Us Dr. Apa Our Team Our Locations Brand PartnersOur Work Before/After Photos Patient Testimonials Buzz BlogSchedule a Consultation How Long Do Porcelain Veneers Last? Aug 6, 2026 One of the most common questions we hear from prospective patients is, “How long do porcelain veneers last?” It’s a reasonable question, but it begins with an assumption that doesn’t accurately reflect exceptional cosmetic dentistry. Patients are often looking for a number—a date on the calendar when their veneers will need to be replaced. The reality is far more nuanced. When designed thoughtfully, executed conservatively, and maintained properly, porcelain veneers are not created with an expiration date in mind. They are designed to become part of a long-term commitment to your oral health, facial aesthetics, and overall well-being. The longevity of a smile makeover depends less on a predetermined timeline and more on the partnership between patient and provider. The Lifespan of Porcelain Veneers Isn’t Defined by a Calendar Porcelain veneers are among the most durable restorations available in cosmetic dentistry. With proper care, they can last around 15 years, and many patients enjoy exceptional results even beyond that. But focusing solely on the number of years misses the larger point. The goal of world-class cosmetic dentistry is not simply to create a beautiful smile that lasts for a fixed period of time. It is to create a smile that continues to function well, support oral health, and complement the face for decades. That requires ongoing stewardship, because exceptional results deserve exceptional care. Just as you wouldn’t expect your skin, body, or hair to maintain themselves indefinitely without attention, your smile is no different. We like to say that oral care is self-care, and maintaining great dentistry is simply part of maintaining yourself. A Smile Makeover Is an Investment in Yourself The most discerning patients understand that aesthetic refinement is never a one-time event. Whether it’s strength training, personalized skincare, or a thoughtfully designed wellness routine, the highest standards of personal care are built through consistency and discipline. They aren’t maintained because something is wrong; they’re maintained because the investment is worth protecting. Your smile deserves the same philosophy. The moment your veneers are placed, you’re making a long-term commitment to prioritizing your oral health. The care that follows isn’t an obligation created by porcelain veneers; it’s a natural extension of protecting something crafted with extraordinary precision. Porcelain Veneers Offer More Than Cosmetic Improvement While porcelain veneers are often associated with creating a more beautiful smile, their benefits extend well beyond aesthetics. When designed by an experienced cosmetic dentist using minimally invasive techniques, veneers can improve the relationship between the teeth, gums, lips, and facial structure in ways that influence both appearance and function. Supporting Natural Facial Architecture The teeth provide important structural support for the lips and surrounding soft tissues. Thoughtfully restoring ideal tooth shape, position, and volume can subtly improve facial balance, creating a more youthful and harmonious appearance without looking artificial. Improving Bite Function A properly designed smile makeover isn’t simply cosmetic. Every restoration is engineered to work within the patient’s bite, helping distribute forces evenly across the teeth and reducing unnecessary stress on the jaw joints and surrounding musculature. Apa Aesthetic is known for making teeth that look and function like natural teeth. When evaluating cosmetic dentistry, it’s impossible to judge a smile on aesthetics alone. A smile may look beautiful, but if it isn’t engineered to function properly, it isn’t finished. Preserving Long-Term Oral Health Precision matters. When veneers are crafted to fit seamlessly against the natural tooth and surrounding gum tissue, they create an environment that is easier to keep healthy. Healthy gums and stable teeth are the foundation of long-term oral wellness, and maintaining that foundation benefits far more than your smile alone. How to Make Porcelain Veneers Last Patients often ask what they need to do to extend the lifespan of their veneers. Maintaining porcelain veneers shouldn’t feel complicated, but it does require consistency. Long-term success depends on: Maintaining excellent daily oral hygiene. Visiting your dentist regularly for professional examinations and cleanings. Wearing a nightguard if recommended. Addressing any changes in your bite or oral health before they become larger problems. Continuing care with a provider who understands your smile and how it was designed. These habits protect not only the porcelain restorations themselves but also the natural teeth supporting them. Why Long-Term Relationships Matter in Cosmetic Dentistry At Apa Aesthetic, we often say that the smile makeover is only the beginning of the relationship. Exceptional cosmetic dentistry continues through routine maintenance, preventive care, and ongoing collaboration between doctor and patient. This philosophy is one of the many reasons our smile makeovers are supported by comprehensive general dentistry. The long-term health of every restoration depends on the long-term health of the entire mouth. Beautiful dentistry is never viewed as a finished product. It is cared for, monitored, and refined over time. The Real Return on Investment The most immediate result of a smile makeover is visual, but the most meaningful results happen gradually. Patients often notice improved confidence, more natural facial support, greater comfort when speaking and chewing, and a smile that becomes so integrated into who they are that they stop thinking about it altogether. As Dr. Michael Apa has long emphasized, exceptional cosmetic dentistry is never just about changing teeth. It is about improving the structural foundation of the smile in a way that elevates both health and aesthetics. That is why the better question isn’t, “When will my veneers expire?” It’s, “How do I preserve a smile designed to last?” Experience World-Class Cosmetic Dentistry At Apa Aesthetic, every smile is individually designed using minimally invasive principles, advanced digital planning, and handcrafted porcelain restorations that prioritize both long-term function and timeless aesthetics. Schedule a consultation at Apa Aesthetic New York, Apa Aesthetic Los Angeles, Apa Aesthetic Miami, or Apa Aesthetic Dubai to discover what’s possible when cosmetic dentistry is approached as both an art and a lifelong investment. pages.title: The Reality of Prepless Veneers - Apa Aesthetic
pages.description: Few phrases in cosmetic dentistry sound more appealing than "prepless veneers." No drilling. No removal of natural tooth structure. A stunning smile with nothing taken away. It's a tempting offer. It's also, in most cases, not the full story. What Are Prepless Veneers, and Who Are They For? Prepless veneers…
pages.text: <!DOCTYPE html> The Reality of Prepless Veneers - Apa Aesthetic What We Do The Apa Experience Cosmetic Dentistry Porcelain Veneers Smile Makeover ProcessWho We Are About Us Dr. Apa Our Team Our Locations Brand PartnersOur Work Before/After Photos Patient Testimonials Buzz BlogSchedule a Consultation The Reality of Prepless Veneers Jul 24, 2026 Few phrases in cosmetic dentistry sound more appealing than “prepless veneers.” No drilling. No removal of natural tooth structure. A stunning smile with nothing taken away. It’s a tempting offer. It’s also, in most cases, not the full story. What Are Prepless Veneers, and Who Are They For? Prepless veneers are exactly what their name suggests: veneers placed directly onto the tooth surface without any preparation of the underlying enamel. No reduction. No shaping. The veneer simply bonds to whatever is already there. In the right situation, prepless veneers can work. But the right situation is far narrower than most patients realize. To be a strong candidate for prepless veneers, several conditions must be met simultaneously. The tooth has to be free of decay, the color change required has to be minimal, and the position of the tooth must be close to ideal already. If any of those factors change, the entire approach loses its viability. On a full arch, all of those conditions being true at the same time is rare. Not impossible, but rare. Why Do So Many Dentists Offer Prepless Veneers? Here’s where the honest conversation gets uncomfortable. Prepless veneers are, in Dr. Apa’s words, more of a marketing tactic than a clinical solution. They sound good in a consultation and ease a patient’s anxiety about the procedure. They also allow a dentist to say something that feels comforting: “we’re not going to touch your teeth at all.” The issue with prepless veneers is what that promise could cost the patient in terms of the final outcome. If a tooth’s position needs adjustment, prepless veneers cannot achieve that cleanly. The incisal edge, the biting edge of the tooth, cannot be repositioned without preparation. That means one of two things happens: either the veneer ends up with an unnaturally thick incisal edge, or it creates a bite interference. Neither outcome serves the patient. Both are entirely predictable before the case even begins. Does Minimal Preparation Actually Harm Your Teeth? This is the core question in the prepless veneer debate, and it deserves a direct answer. The amount of tooth structure removed in a minimal preparation for veneers is, in Dr. Apa’s description, next to nothing. When done correctly, it’s a tiny reduction with no meaningful impact on the long term health of the dentition. And yet, that minimal preparation makes an enormous difference in what the final result can achieve. It gives the ceramist room to work. It allows the tooth’s position to be adjusted. It creates the conditions for a veneer that fits naturally, functions properly, and looks the way the patient envisioned when they first sat down for the consultation. Although “prepless veneers” sounds like a patient is getting the best of both worlds, it’s important to note: both prepless and minimally prepped veneers are permanent. Once bonded, the tooth is committed to a veneer for life. While the restorations themselves generally last 15–20 years before replacement is needed, the tooth will continue to require a veneer regardless of which technique was used. The real question is not whether preparation harms the tooth. It is whether skipping that preparation is worth the compromises it forces on the result. And in the vast majority of cases, the honest answer is no. What Should You Ask Before Agreeing to Prepless Veneers? During the consultation process, it’s important for your provider to distinguish between whether prepless veneers are the best choice for your case, or if they simply believe the phrase will encourage you to sign the treatement plan. If they decide to go in the direction of preless veneers, ask what compromises, if any, will be made to your final smile design by avoiding preparation. Ask whether the position of your teeth needs to change, and if so, how prepless veneers will accommodate that without creating thickness or interference at the incisal edge. A provider who prioritizes your actual outcome will answer those questions directly. They will tell you if, in your case, prepless veneers are not only possible, but the right amount for you. They will not lead with the prepless option simply because it is easier to sell. The goal is a result that looks right, functions properly, and holds up for fifteen plus years. If that means prepless veneers are the best path forward, great. If it means conservative preparations are necessary, also great. The most important decision you will make in your smile makeover journey is who your provider is. Choose once, and choose well. Knowing your best path forward is exactly what you should expect from the person designing your smile. Are you ready to begin your journey at Apa Aesthetic? pages.title: The Center of Expression: A New Philosophy of the Smile - Apa Aesthetic
pages.description: We tend to look at the eyes as the window to a person’s internal world, but it is the lower third of the face that handles the actual mechanics of human connection. It is where we speak, where we laugh, and where we betray our truest emotions.  At Apa Aesthetic,…
headings: The Center of Expression: A New Philosophy of the Smile
pages.text: <!DOCTYPE html> The Center of Expression: A New Philosophy of the Smile - Apa Aesthetic What We Do The Apa Experience Cosmetic Dentistry Porcelain Veneers Smile Makeover ProcessWho We Are About Us Dr. Apa Our Team Our Locations Brand PartnersOur Work Before/After Photos Patient Testimonials Buzz BlogSchedule a Consultation The Center of Expression: A New Philosophy of the Smile Jul 10, 2026 We tend to look at the eyes as the window to a person’s internal world, but it is the lower third of the face that handles the actual mechanics of human connection. It is where we speak, where we laugh, and where we betray our truest emotions. At Apa Aesthetic, our team doesn’’t view a smile as an isolated set of teeth to be repaired. We view it as the anchor of your entire presentation. Feeling good about yourself doesn’t have to be something you put off. It can be something you feel everyday. “I Don’t Like My Smile” It starts small. A chipped tooth. A gap you tell yourself you’ll fix someday. But, someday gets pushed further away, and in the meantime, you become stuck under your smile’s control. When someone is self-conscious about their teeth, they don’t just stop smiling; they fundamentally alter how they communicate. You learn to talk with a slightly tighter jaw. You master the “social smirk” – that polite, lips-pressed-together greeting that acts as a shield. When you laugh, your hand automatically flies up to cover your mouth, an instinctive reflex born out of a desire to protect yourself from being seen. If you’re reading this and know these behaviors well, this is your sign. The constant, subconscious policing of your own face is exhausting. It means you are never fully present in a room because a fraction of your brain is always playing defense, tracking angles, lighting, and proximity. It isn’t just your teeth that are hidden. Your entire personality is being filtered through an insecurity. “I Don’t Care About My Teeth” It’s not laziness. It’s avoidance. When your teeth feel like a flaw, the dentist’s office becomes a place of dread. The mirror is a reminder of a deep longing for something more. The gap between where you are and where you want to be feels too vast to close, so you stop trying to close it at all. It’s a patient our practice knows well. Someone who cares about their teeth, but has been slowly defeated by years of feeling insecure. Someone who had learned to smile without really smiling. Can Fixing Your Teeth Change Your Life? It’s a question no one asks when they talk about dentistry. For anyone who has sat in the Apa Aesthetic chair and seen the results, the answer is a resounding yes. When the smile finally reflects the person behind it, the change is undeniable. Patients who walked in with their lips pressed together walk out differently. They carry themselves differently. They speak differently. They express joy differently. As Dr. Apa explains: “You get their teeth and bite looking good, you get them feeling good, and then it’s a different person coming into your office.” That change is not only cosmetic. It is deeply, fundamentally human. What Does Restorative Dentistry Really Mean? Clinically, restorative dentistry is about enhancing function. Rebuilding the bite. Strengthening the structure. Ensuring health. Restoration, in its fullest sense, means restoring more than just teeth. It’s about restoring confidence. The courage to be seen. The freedom to laugh without hesitation. Restoring the small, everyday moments most people take for granted: a genuine laugh, a confident photograph, a conversation where you’re not quietly monitoring your expression. This is what Dr. Apa means when he says that restorative dentistry changes lives. Not as a marketing claim, but as a truth he witnesses in his practice every single day. Why Does Apa Aesthetic Exist? Most clinics measure success by the numbers: The shade match, the precision of the margins, the symmetry. And while those things matter deeply, there’s more value than what meets the eye. At Apa Aesthetic, we return to a simpler question. Did our patient leave feeling like themselves again? Not just their teeth fixed. Not just their bite aligned. Did the person who walked in with pressed lips and years of quiet shame walk out with a smile on their face? When the answer is yes, we’ve done our job. That is what it means to practice cosmetic restorative dentistry, and it’s what so many dentists miss. Are you ready to begin your journey at Apa Aesthetic? headings: The Conversation Missing From Dental School
pages.text: <!DOCTYPE html> The Conversation Missing From Dental School - Apa Aesthetic What We Do The Apa Experience Cosmetic Dentistry Porcelain Veneers Smile Makeover ProcessWho We Are About Us Dr. Apa Our Team Our Locations Brand PartnersOur Work Before/After Photos Patient Testimonials Buzz BlogSchedule a Consultation The Conversation Missing From Dental School Jul 6, 2026 There’s no shortage of conversations in dentistry about technique. Every conference, lecture, and continuing education course dives into materials, workflows, preparation design, and the latest technology. Those things matter. They’re the foundation. But they’re only part of the job. When Dr. Apa recently spoke to a room of NYU dental students, he spent surprisingly little time talking about dentistry itself and made a deliberate choice to shift the conversation to one about people. Long before a patient becomes a clinical case, they’re a person who’s been thinking about their smile for years. Whether they recognize it or not, they’ve learned how to smile a certain way. They’ve avoided cameras. They’ve convinced themselves that no one notices. When they sit in your chair, they’re not just asking for better teeth. They’re trusting you with something much bigger: their confidence. That’s the part that isn’t taught often enough. What Does It Mean to Change Someone’s Life? One question came up throughout the conversation, and it’s one that Dr. Apa puts directly to anyone entering the profession. Are you making the patient feel good, or are you making yourself feel good? It’s an uncomfortable distinction, but an important one. As clinicians, it’s easy to become attached to technical perfection, and there is a version of doing good dental work that is fundamentally about the dentist. The satisfaction of a flawless preparation. The pride of a result that looks stunning in a photo. The professional validation of a case that any peer would praise as technically excellent. Those things matter. But they aren’t the finish line. The work isn’t complete until the patient sees themselves differently. Until the smile feels like it belongs to them. Until they leave more confident than when they arrived. A technically flawless case that doesn’t connect with the person wearing it misses the point. Those are two entirely different outcomes. The best clinicians understand that dentistry is never just about teeth. Building the Next Generation That philosophy is why our commitment to education extends far beyond the lecture hall. The Apa Aesthetic Suite at NYU College of Dentistry was created to give students a place where clinical excellence and aesthetic thinking come together. It’s an opportunity to see how treatment planning, communication, artistry, and technical execution all influence the final outcome. The Apa Suite is only the beginning. Our upcoming Design x Hand curriculum takes that learning further through hands-on education, giving clinicians the opportunity to join likeminded dentists and work alongside Dr. Apa and our team while refining the details that can’t be learned from slides alone. The foundation of good dentistry is technique. Great dentistry is built on judgment. Observation. Communication. And understanding the responsibility that comes with every patient who sits in your chair. Those are the lessons that stay with you long after graduation. What the Best Dental Education Actually Teaches During his student years, Dr. Apa founded the Aesthetic Dental Society at NYU, and his motivation was the same one that he carries through every case, lecture, and symposium: that the most important lessons in this profession are not always the ones formally taught. That the patient in your chair has a life story. That your job is to understand it well enough to serve the patient’s future smile. That the communication happening before you touch a single tooth is as important as anything that happens after. That the standard worth chasing isn’t a only a technically perfect result, It’s a person who leaves your care feeling genuinely better about themselves. Why Does This Matter to Patients? The dentist across from you at a consultation is making a choice, consciously or not, about whose experience they are centered on. The best ones have made that choice intentionally. They have decided that the patient’s happiness is the finish line, not their own satisfaction with the clinical outcome. They ask different questions, listen differently, and plan differently because of it. A result that looks perfect on paper but doesn’t feel right to the person wearing it is not a success. A patient who leaves quietly uncertain, who smiles less freely than they hoped, who feels like something was done to them rather than for them, represents a miss regardless of how precise the margins are. The dentists worth seeking out are the ones who understand that distinction and let it guide every decision they make, from the first consultation to the final result. Not because it makes them feel good as clinicians. Because it makes the person in the chair feel good as a human being. That is the Apa Aesthetic standard. Are you willing to demand it? Are you ready to begin your journey at Apa Aesthetic? Schedule a consultation at Apa Aesthetic New York, Apa Aesthetic Los Angeles, Apa Aesthetic Miami, or Apa Aesthetic Dubai, and experience your own life-changing transformation. Still Curious? How Much Do Veneers Actually Cost?
Why Do People Put Off Fixing Their Smile?
What Makes Apa Aesthetic Different From Other Cosmetic Dentists?
pages.text: <!DOCTYPE html> Is Your Smile Part of Your Self-Care Routine? - Apa Aesthetic What We Do The Apa Experience Cosmetic Dentistry Porcelain Veneers Smile Makeover ProcessWho We Are About Us Dr. Apa Our Team Our Locations Brand PartnersOur Work Before/After Photos Patient Testimonials Buzz BlogSchedule a Consultation Is Your Smile Part of Your Self-Care Routine? Jun 12, 2026 There’s a version of self-care that’s agreed upon without question. We’ll spend on the hair treatments, the high-end skincare regimens, and the curated wardrobe in the name of looking and feeling like the best version of ourselves. We invest instinctively, until it comes to our smiles; that’s where the psychology shifts, the conversation changes, and hesitation begins to set in. At Apa Aesthetic, we believe your smile shouldn’t be an afterthought. How Much Do Veneers Actually Cost? When people hesitate to invest in their smile, it’s usually not because of the number – it’s just how they’re looking at it. We’re used to spending money on temporary beauty and lifestyle routines that we don’t even realize what those figures add up to. Between top-tier salon appointments, high-performance clinical skincare, and regular wellness treatments, the annual investment to maintain your baseline profile easily reaches five figures. Over fifteen years, it represents a significant, compounding expenditure on assets that require constant touch-ups just to remain level. By that time, you’re looking at a six figure+ investment. On hair cut, color, and styling alone, after spending $700 to $900 per appointment (roughly $3,000) annually between four visits, your 15-year spend is around $45,000; the same price of a smile makeover that lasts 15 years. The numbers are remarkably similar. The only difference is efficiency. One is a perpetual maintenance cycle; the other is a singular aesthetic investment that pays visual dividends every single day, with zero ongoing upkeep. Are Veneers Worth the Investment? In the worlds of fine tailoring and high jewelry, value is dictated by longevity and presence. We invest in pieces that stand the test of time and elevate everything else we wear. Your smile is one of the only assets you’ll wear every second of your life. Unlike a wardrobe that rotates or an exotic vehicle that depreciates, a masterfully crafted smile is working for you constantly. In the boardroom, on a global stage, or in a spontaneous photograph, it communicates an effortless refinement and a quiet confidence before you ever say a word. It is your most prominent personal trademark. Every moment you walk into a room, your smile speaks before you do. Our patients consistently tell us that the true return on investment goes far beyond the mirror. It is a profound shift in presence. They navigate negotiations with a renewed sense of authority. They stop hiding their laughter. They show up differently, professionally and personally. A beautiful smile communicates confidence before you say a single word. That kind of return doesn’t fade between appointments. When you invest in your smile, you are securing a lasting aesthetic foundation. Why Do People Put Off Fixing Their Smile? Most patients come to us having never considered their smile as their self-care routine. They’ve spent years investing freely in their skin, their hair, and their wardrobes, while quietly hoping the discomfort would fade on its own. Hesitation carries a cost. It chips away at your ability to be fully present and laugh openly. Dr. Apa frequently posts a foundational question to people navigating the decision to pursue a smile makeover: How much would you pay each year to look in the mirror and genuinely love your smile? For most people, the answer is immediate; people realize they’ve compromised on their most expressive feature, and the hesitation disappears. What Makes Apa Aesthetic Different From Other Cosmetic Dentists? A premium set of porcelain veneers, crafted and placed by an experienced cosmetic dentist, lasts approximately 15 to 20 years. That means the investment you make today carries you through 15 years of confidence. We understand that any significant investment deserves trust. That’s why our process is built around transparency, personalization, and results that speak for themselves. Nearly 70% of our patients travel to one of our offices specifically for the Apa Aesthetic level of care. Why? Because they understand that exceptional cosmetic dentistry isn’t something you can find by searching “dentist near me.” It’s a specialty. It’s an art form. And it’s a decision that, when made with the right provider, changes everything. We reject the one-size-fits-all approach. We analyze the unique architecture of your entire face, designing a bespoke smile that complements your features. We are not just changing teeth; we are redefining aesthetics. Your Smile Deserves to Be Part of Your Routine Your smile is already a part of who you are. At Apa Aesthetic, we simply help you become the best version of yourself. Are you ready to begin your journey at Apa Aesthetic? At Apa Aesthetic, we believe that exceptional smile design is about more than clinical technique – it’s about vision, communication, artistry, and execution. After more than 25 years of refining our approach to comprehensive aesthetic dentistry, we are proud to introduce Design X Hand, a progressive educational series created to bridge the gap between learning and mastery. Design X Hand was developed for practitioners who want more than lectures and theory. It is designed for clinicians actively treating patients who are seeking practical, real-world systems they can implement immediately. Every course is rooted in the workflows, protocols, and philosophies that have been refined through thousands of cases and decades of collaboration between doctors, patients, and laboratory teams. Participation begins with the Apa Symposium, the cornerstone of the Design X Hand experience. The symposium establishes the foundation upon which all future training is built, providing attendees with a comprehensive understanding of smile design principles, treatment planning, preparation strategies, provisionalization, material selection, and the communication systems necessary to achieve predictable outcomes. More importantly, it introduces the mindset required to approach esthetic cases with confidence, clarity, and purpose. Apa Symposium attendees will gain access to a series of progressively advanced educational opportunities. The first level will feature hands-on training on models, allowing participants to develop and refine their preparation techniques, create temporaries and direct provisionals, and implement the clinical workflows discussed during the symposium. Future programs will expand to include laboratory-focused education for ceramists and technicians, fostering a deeper understanding of the collaborative relationship that drives successful aesthetic dentistry. The culmination of the Design X Hand curriculum will be immersive live-patient experiences, where clinicians and laboratory teams work together through every stage of treatment – from case design and material selection to creation, insertion, and final delivery. Participants will gain firsthand exposure to the nuances that define exceptional results, including ceramic selection, translucency, optical properties, and the clinical decision-making that transforms good dentistry into extraordinary dentistry. Design X Hand is more than a course series. It is a pathway to clinical excellence built on experience, mentorship, and practical application. By creating a structured progression from foundational concepts to real-world patient treatment, we are offering a unique opportunity to learn the systems, mindset, and techniques that have defined our approach to esthetic dentistry for more than two decades. If you’re an Apa Symposium attendee and want to learn more, visit DesignXhand.com and @designxhand. headings: Can Cosmetic Dentistry Fix Crooked Teeth?
The Emotional Weight Behind a Smile
Should You Travel for Porcelain Veneers?
The True Beauty of Restorative Cosmetic Dentistry
pages.text: <!DOCTYPE html> Can Cosmetic Dentistry Fix Crooked Teeth? - Apa Aesthetic What We Do The Apa Experience Cosmetic Dentistry Porcelain Veneers Smile Makeover ProcessWho We Are About Us Dr. Apa Our Team Our Locations Brand PartnersOur Work Before/After Photos Patient Testimonials Buzz BlogSchedule a Consultation Can Cosmetic Dentistry Fix Crooked Teeth? May 22, 2026 For many adults, the decision to improve their smile begins with a simple goal: to feel more confident. When patients finally decide to take that step, their minds almost automatically jump to the same solution: braces. For most, orthodontics is what patients grew up seeing, hearing about, and experiencing as kids. Metal brackets and rubber bands were the universal rite of passage for fixing teeth. Today, treatments like Invisalign and other clear aligner systems have become widely accessible, with many general dental practices offering orthodontic treatment despite limited specialty training beyond the certification courses required by the aligned companies. When patients notice their adult smiles changing, typically after years of feeling self-conscious about worn, uneven, or aging teeth, they default to what they know. If something feels “off,” the instinct is often, “I guess I need braces or Invisalign.” Increasingly, adult patients are discovering a frustrating truth: true smile transformation is about far more than simply moving teeth. In fact, relying on childhood solutions for adult dental problems can sometimes leave your smile in a much worse position than when you started. Take it from one of Dr. Apa’s patients who describes spending years in orthodontic treatment, only to feel as though the process was moving further away from the result she envisioned. It’s a sentiment many patients are hesitant to say aloud, but its a reality that we see every day at Apa Aesthetic. Patients begin treatment believing there is only one path forward, even when their instincts tell them something feels incomplete. Cosmetic restorative dentistry offers something many patients have never been told before: there is another way. What Is Advanced Cosmetic Dentistry? Apa Aesthetic approaches smile makeovers at the intersection of restorative dentistry, facial aesthetics, digital precision, and deeply individualized care. Every smile is designed with consideration not only for the teeth themselves, but for the harmony of the entire face. Exceptional cosmetic dentistry is never defined by the whiteness or uniformity of a smile alone. It is balance. Proportion. Softness. Character. It is the way the smile supports the lips, complements the eyes, enhances facial structure, and functions naturally within the bite. The most beautiful cosmetic dentistry is often the kind that feels effortless – refined rather than obvious. At Apa Aesthetic, subtlety is everything. We’ve done our job well when a patient walks down the street, and someone says, “You look incredible,” without immediately identifying why. The compliment should be about their glow, their confidence, their overall presence; a signal of restored teeth that look like teeth. Feeling Understood By Your Provider Our patient had been in orthodontia for six years, and her dentist said that she had one more year to go. She was seeing a “general dentist who does ortho.” Just as patients seeking comprehensive cosmetic dentistry should look for a dentist who performs an elite level of aesthetic (and functionally sound) work every single day, patients considering orthodontic treatment should seek out an orthodontist. In highly nuanced areas of dentistry, specialization matters. Patients often spend years trying to explain discomfort, frustration, or dissatisfaction with their smile. Sometimes they are told to simply continue treatment. “It will get better,” they’re told, with no end in sight. Sometimes they begin to doubt their own instincts altogether. The best cosmetic dentists are not simply evaluating teeth. At Apa Aesthetic, we hear our patients’ stories, understand their concerns, study the nuances of their facial structure and bite, and identify solutions that align with both function and aesthetics. Our smile makeovers are designed to enhance natural beauty. After cosmetic dentistry, patients are no longer chasing incremental improvements. No more band-aid fixes. Finally, the entire picture comes together. The Emotional Weight Behind a Smile “People don’t realize the story behind the teeth and what it takes to get there,” our patient shares. Behind nearly every smile transformation is a deeply personal story. Years of hiding teeth in photographs. Smiling cautiously in conversations. Feeling frustrated after previous dental experiences. Wanting desperately to feel comfortable again in their own skin. A smile carries enormous emotional significance. It influences the way we communicate, the way we present ourselves professionally, and the way we experience confidence in everyday life. It’s only one of the reasons cosmetic restorative dentistry has become increasingly meaningful for adult patients. Many are not looking for perfection. They are looking for relief from insecurity, discomfort, and years of feeling disconnected from their appearance. When treatment is thoughtfully planned and artistically executed, the transformation extends well beyond aesthetics. Patients speak more confidently. They stop covering their mouths when they laugh. They feel more at ease socially and professionally. Most importantly, they feel like themselves again. That is the power of smile makeovers. Should You Travel for Porcelain Veneers? As cosmetic dentistry has evolved, so has the level of discernment among patients seeking smile transformation. “A lot of people are like, ‘Why are you going so far?’” our patient explains. “And it’s like, well, this [result] is why.” Today, nearly 70% of Apa Aesthetic patients travel to one of our offices for treatment – a reflection of how intentional patients have become when choosing a cosmetic dentist. More than ever, patients understand that exceptional cosmetic restorative dentistry is not simply a routine dental procedure. It is a highly specialized blend of aesthetic artistry, advanced restorative dentistry, facial harmony, bite function, and long-term oral health. As a result, patients are no longer limiting their search to Google searches of “cosmetic dentist near me,” and choosing the first result. Instead, they are actively seeking out providers whose expertise, philosophy, and results align with the level of care they want to receive; the kind of care provided at Apa Aesthetic. Smile makeovers are both a science and an art form. The difference between a good cosmetic dental result and an exceptional one often lies in the subtle details invisible to the untrained eye: tooth proportion, facial balance, bite alignment, texture, translucency, and the ability to create a smile that feels naturally beautiful rather than overly treated. Advanced cosmetic dentistry requires technical precision, aesthetic judgment, restraint, and a deep understanding of long-term function. It requires a cosmetic restorative dentist who sees the smile as part of the entire face – not as an isolated set of teeth. For many patients who have spent years searching for answers, traveling to Apa Aesthetic for cosmetic restorative dentistry feels like finally finding clarity, confidence, and a treatment approach designed specifically for them. The True Beauty of Restorative Cosmetic Dentistry There is a misconception that cosmetic dentistry is purely elective or superficial. In reality, the best cosmetic restorative work is profoundly functional and deeply personal. A properly restored smile can improve bite stability, comfort, speech, oral health, and longevity while simultaneously creating a more youthful, harmonious appearance.
